A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, all four figures and four tables, and Appendices A-D. No material gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports 15 original coding experiments across three systems, quantitative evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix D, and participant-interview findings in Section 6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original coding experiments, quantitative results in Tables 1, 2, and 4 and Figure 4, and participant-interview findings.

M1.justification: The three interactive coding procedures and the theme-matching and evaluation framework in Sections 3-5 and Appendices A, B, and D are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same approximately 85,000 US COVID-19 vaccine tweets and evaluate synchronous and asynchronous qualitative coding with the same participant population.

E2.justification: The evaluated systems remain those of Fang et al. (2023), Pacheco et al. (2023), and Chew et al. (2023). Their participation in the reported comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain three individual asynchronous and two three-person synchronous experiments per system, the same metrics, initial partitions, and 1,200-pair post-hoc evaluation. Appendix settings also match.

E4.justification: The top-25% document analysis, correctness analysis by document relatedness, and qualitative interview analyses are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the unpaired t-tests and significance markers in Tables 1-2 and Krippendorff's alpha of 0.632. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4, Figure 4, and interview findings match. For example, Table 1 retains topic-model Jaccard similarities of 0.56 for synchronous and 0.30 for asynchronous coding.

T1.justification: The definitions and calculations for theme matching, consistency, cohesiveness, and distinctiveness are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: studying collaboration effects across three systems and proposing an evaluation framework for coding quality.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations linking interaction capabilities to benefits from synchronous deliberation, the same recommendations, and all four limitations in Section 8.

D1.justification: Appendices A-D retain identical hyperparameters, operational details, interview instructions, LLM hardware/runtime information, and prompts. Section 9's planned release of annotation results and analysis code is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged, including the argument that prior system evaluations insufficiently address different collaboration settings.

P1.justification: v3 adds Rohan Das with an equal-contribution marker and email address, and updates the arXiv version/date. The research prose and section and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page author/contact lines expand, and small typographic spacing differences occur elsewhere. Figures, table structures, captions, and their locations remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 changes authorship/contact information and minor typesetting while preserving the study design, results, interpretations, limitations, and appendix documentation. These edits establish no meaningful net difference in scientific rigor, completeness, or clarity.
